chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the soft leather shoe (khuff); one goes to the market and buys the shoe, not knowing whether it is tanned or not. What do you say about praying in it, while he does not know if he should pray in it? He said, 'Yes, I buy the shoe from the market, it is made for me, and I pray in it, and it is not upon you to ask (about the tanning).'

key_terms.الْخُفَّ: The shoe (specifically the type worn for prayer/wudu)
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَةُ: The question/requirement (implying the burden of inquiry)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to check if my leather shoes are tanned before praying in them?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of prayer in leather shoes (khuff) does not depend on the buyer's certainty regarding the tanning process, reflecting the Shia principle of *istishab* (presumption of purity) in the absence of contrary evidence. He further clarifies that this ruling applies even if the shoes are custom-made, emphasizing that the obligation of verification is lifted for the general believer, thereby simplifying the conditions for valid prayer attire.
